examples: The pond has ice.
Put ice in the drink.
The ice is cold.
Ice covered the pond all winter.
She put ice in her lemonade.
The road was slippery with ice.

easy.def: A huge block of ice floating in the sea.
examples: An iceberg floated by.
The iceberg is big.
The ship passed an iceberg.

more.def: A very large piece of ice that has broken off from a glacier and floats in the sea, with most of it hidden under the water.
examples: The ship steered clear of the huge iceberg in the cold sea.
Only a small part of an iceberg shows above the water.
Polar bears sometimes rest on an iceberg.

easy.def: An old name for a refrigerator.
examples: The milk is in the icebox.
Grandpa had an icebox.
Put it in the icebox.

more.def: A box or cabinet that was filled with ice to keep food cold, used before refrigerators; also an old name for a refrigerator.
examples: Before electric refrigerators, families kept milk and butter in an icebox filled with ice.
Grandma still calls the refrigerator the icebox.
The milk was kept cold in the icebox.

easy.def: A ship that breaks through ice, or a game to meet people.
examples: The icebreaker cut through ice.
We played an icebreaker.
The icebreaker is strong.

more.def: A ship made to break through ice, or a game that helps people meet each other.
examples: An icebreaker cleared a path through the frozen sea.
We played an icebreaker on the first day.
The icebreaker pushed through thick ice.
I drank iced tea.
She had an iced drink.
We ate iced cookies.

more.def: Served very cold with ice, or covered with icing.
examples: She ordered an iced tea on the hot summer day.
He ate an iced cookie with pink frosting.
The iced lemonade was cool and sweet.

easy.def: A long, pointed piece of ice that hangs down.
examples: An icicle hung from the roof.
The icicle dripped.
I saw an icicle.

more.def: A long, pointed piece of ice made by dripping water that freezes.
examples: An icicle hung from the edge of the roof.
The icicle melted in the sun.
Icicles sparkled on the branches.

easy.def: The sweet, creamy topping on a cake.
examples: I like pink icing.
The cake has white icing.
She licked the icing off the spoon.

more.def: A sweet, soft topping that is spread on cakes and cookies.
examples: She spread pink icing over the cupcakes.
The cookies were covered in thick, sweet icing.
He licked the chocolate icing from the spoon.
The mud is icky.
I do not like icky food.
The icky goo is on my hand.

more.def: Unpleasant and sticky, or making you feel that something is gross.
examples: The icky mud stuck to my shoes.
The icky smell came from the old milk.
I did not want to touch the icky slime.

easy.def: A small picture on a screen that stands for something.
examples: Tap the icon.
The icon is a heart.
I clicked the icon.

more.def: A small picture on a computer or phone screen that you press to open a program, or a famous person or thing that stands for something.
examples: Tap the camera icon to take a picture.
The icon for the music app looks like a note.
The Statue of Liberty is an icon of freedom.

easy.def: Very famous and a symbol of something.
examples: The tower is iconic.
An iconic song.
The iconic building.

more.def: Very famous and seen as a symbol of something.
examples: The Eiffel Tower is an iconic landmark.
It is an iconic song that everyone knows.
The iconic bridge appears on postcards.

easy.def: Covered with ice, or very cold.
examples: The road was icy.
The wind is icy.
An icy pond.

more.def: Covered with ice, or extremely cold.
examples: The icy road made the cars slide.
An icy wind blew across the frozen lake.
She dipped her toes in the icy water and gasped.
